summary: Laguna Beach packs roughly 23,000 residents into just under ten square miles, yet those square miles are so dramatically carved by coastal canyons that two addresses a half-mile apart can differ by hundreds of feet in elevation — the geography simultaneously delivers Pacific sunset panoramas from ridgeline roads and tucked-away canyon bottoms where you lose cell signal. The setting is genuinely vertical: Pacific Coast Highway threads between sandstone bluffs and steep hillsides, and trails like those in Laguna Coast Wilderness Park put thousands of acres of protected open space within a short drive of downtown. That downtown — anchored by a compact stretch of gallery-lined streets, independent restaurants, and summer institutions like the Pageant of the Masters and the Sawdust Art Festival — gives the town an identity so specific it resists comparison. But the tradeoffs are equally sharp: a median home value exceeding $2 million against a median household income of about $140,500 yields a price-to-income ratio above 14, meaning purchasing requires substantial wealth beyond local earnings alone. Rents averaging $2,802 a month are steep but less absurd relative to income. The town is not a major employment center — most working residents commute north toward Irvine's tech and healthcare corridors — and PCH becomes a bottleneck in summer when visitor traffic swells. Year-round highs averaging 69°F with over nine hours of daily sunshine make the climate remarkably even, rarely hot and almost never cold. Laguna Beach is a place where the physical beauty is extraordinary and the cost of accessing it daily is a number most households in the country would find surreal.
